subject: gk
question: How many writs are guaranteed under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to move to the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution.

• Article 32 provides for five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.

• These writs are designed to enforce the fundamental rights of citizens against arbitrary actions of the state and other public authorities.

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Habeas Corpus:**

• This writ is used to release a person who has been unlawfully detained or imprisoned.

• The term "Habeas Corpus" means "to have the body of".

• It is a powerful safeguard against arbitrary detention by the state.

• **Mandamus:**

• This writ is issued by a court to a public official or body to perform a duty they are obligated to perform.

• The term "Mandamus" means "we command".

• It ensures that duties imposed by law are fulfilled.

• **Prohibition:**

• This writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.

• The term "Prohibition" means "to forbid".

• It is used to stop lower courts from proceeding with cases they are not authorized to handle.

• **Quo-Warranto:**

• This writ is used to challenge the legality of a person's claim to a public office.

• The term "Quo-Warranto" means "by what authority".

• It helps ensure that public offices are not usurped by unauthorized persons.

• **Certiorari:**

• This writ is issued by a higher court to review the legality of a decision made by a lower court or tribunal.

• The term "Certiorari" means "to be certified" or "to be informed".

• It is used to correct errors in the proceedings of lower courts and tribunals.

</ul
